Surah At-Taghabun (The Mutual Loss and Gain) [Meccan or Medinan; its verses number eighteen]

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ — it exalts Him above every imperfection. The lam (لِلَّهِ, "to Allah") is here superfluous (zā'idah), and He used "mā" (what) rather than "man" (who) because of the predominance of the majority (taghlīban li'l-aktharī), since most of what is in the heavens and earth is not rational.
﴿He it is who created you; then among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ in the original creation. ﴿Then He causes you to die and restores you to that state﴾.
﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and fashioned you, and made your forms good, and fashioned your forms well﴾, since He made the shape of the human being the best of shapes.

﴿He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And God is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾ (He knows) what is in them (the hearts) of secrets and beliefs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 5:

﴿Has there not come to you﴾, O disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿the news﴾, i.e., the report, ﴿of those who disbelieved before, and they tasted the consequence of their affair﴾, i.e., the punishment for disbelief in this world; ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful (in the Hereafter).

ذَلِكَ (Dhalika) — that, i.e., the punishment of this world.
بِأَنَّهُ — because it (ضَمِير الشَّأْن, the dhamir al-sha'n, the "pronoun of the matter," an anaphoric pronoun referring to the situation that follows).
كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلهمْ بِالبَيِّناتِ — their messengers used to come to them with the clear proofs, the evident arguments for faith.
فَقالُوا أبَشَر — and they said, "Human beings?" — the word is intended in the generic sense (أُرِيدَ بِهِ الجِنْس).
يَهْدُونَنا — "who guide us."
فَكَفَرُوا وتَوَلَّوْا — so they disbelieved and turned away, from faith.
واسْتَغْنى اللَّه — and Allah was self-sufficient, independent of their faith.
واللَّه غَنِيّ — and Allah is Free of need,
حَمِيد — Praiseworthy, praised in His actions.

﴿Those who disbelieve claim that﴾. "أن" is *mukhaffafa* (the lightened form of *inna*, in which the emphatic particle is reduced), and its noun, "مَحْذُوف" (omitted), is left out, meaning: that they [will not be resurrected].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 8:

﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an)

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, on Surah 64, verse 9:

﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾ that is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ the believers will defraud the disbelievers (yaghbinu, "will cheat/defraud") by taking their residences and their families in Paradise, had they believed. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and will admit him﴾ and in another recitation, with the nun (bi-l-nūn) in both verbs (yukaffir and yudkhil).
﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally; and wretched is the destination﴾ it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 11:

﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾ by His decree. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾ in His saying that calamity is by His decree, ﴿He guides his heart﴾ to patience over it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 12:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 15:

﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, distracting you from the matters of the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah has with Him a great reward﴾; so do not forfeit it through your preoccupation with wealth and children.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 16:

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, abrogating His saying ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾. ﴿And listen﴾ to what you are commanded, with the listening of acceptance, ﴿and obey, and spend﴾ in obedience, ﴿it is better for yourselves﴾. The word "khayran" (good) is the predicate of a omitted verb "yakun" (it will be), and it is the answer to the imperative. ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful﴾, meaning the winners.

If you lend Allah a goodly loan (by giving charity wholeheartedly), He will multiply it for you (and in another reading, yudaʿʿifuhu with the doubling of the ʿayn, [multiplying it] for each one [dirham] tenfold up to seven hundred [times] and more), and forgive you, for Allah is Appreciative (shakur), Forbearing (halim) — He rewards obedience, and is Forbearing in punishing disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 64, verse 18:

﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ — the secret; ﴿and the witnessed﴾ — the open; ﴿the Mighty﴾ — in His dominion; ﴿the Wise﴾ — in His creation.
